To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

transposition errors in serial recall are asymmetric, that this asymmetry is independent of report order and recall mode, that it increases with list length, and that it is independent of output position.

(1) transposition errors are more likely when the target item is presented early in a list and the distractor item late, (2) transposition errors occur more frequently than would be predicted by the serial position curve for the list, and (3) the probability of transposition errors increases with list length.
the transposition asymmetry was observed in immediate serial recall and was independent of report mode, cueing condition and output position.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the nature of transposition errors and their relation to other types of memory errors.
the nature of the errors in the immediate serial recall of verbal material and the conditions that produce these errors.
the cognitive mechanisms that underlie the recall of serially ordered information.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the transposition asymmetry in serial recall is a robust phenomenon that can be observed under a wide variety of experimental conditions.
the asymmetry of transpositions is a robust and reliable phenomenon that can be explained by a simple model of serial memory.
transposition errors occur more frequently in early than in late positions of the recall sequence.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the serial order information in memory is not represented in a uniform way.
the serial position curve for immediate serial recall is not only a memory trace but also a production template.

transposition errors in immediate serial recall are asymmetric in the sense that they are more likely to occur too early rather than to late, and that this asymmetry is independent of the recall mode and of output position.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the asymmetry in transposition errors is not due to the output position, the report order or the recall mode.
the transposition asymmetry in serial recall is not an artefact of list length or report order, but is a genuine phenomenon.
the asymmetry of transpositions is a general property of serial recall, independent of report order and output position.
